about: Maritime rescue coordination leads and national emergency lines, published institutional contacts only. Seeded from the maritime medevac assessment Shane supplied on 2026-10-05 (Philippines to Sri Lanka transit), which reviewed each published page on that date and called none of them. OSAP has not called or re-read these pages itself: every entry is 'published, not tested'. These are coordination leads, not a map of rescue jurisdiction; the responsible RCC coordinates cross-border support. Revalidate before sailing.
via: Supplied maritime medevac assessment, 5 October 2026 (contacts reviewed that day, not called)

centres.name: Philippine Coast Guard Command Center
centres.note: Official 2024 charter; the assessment could not fetch the PDF directly and read it from the search index. Confirm current duty access.

centres.name: Singapore MPA Port Operations Control Centre (maritime rescue)
centres.role: Published 24-hour emergency contacts. Singapore's search and rescue region extends into the South China Sea.
centres.srcname: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore: Search and Rescue

centres.name: Malaysia MRCC Putrajaya (MMEA)
centres.role: National maritime rescue coordination. Verify the working duty number.
centres.srcname: Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency: MRCC and MRSC directory
centres.note: Directory versions carry different update dates; these numbers agreed across the versions the assessment read.

centres.name: Malaysia MRSC Langkawi (MMEA)
centres.role: Northern Malacca and nearby regional coordination lead; jurisdiction is assigned by the RCC.
centres.srcname: Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency: MRCC and MRSC directory

centres.name: Malaysia MRSC Johor Bahru (MMEA)
centres.srcname: Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency: MRCC and MRSC directory

centres.name: Malaysia Maritime Communication Centre, Port Klang (Marine Department)
centres.role: Published 24-hour maritime communications and ship-to-shore coordination for injured seafarers.
centres.srcname: Marine Department Malaysia: Malaysia Maritime Communication Centre

centres.name: Indonesia BASARNAS (National Search and Rescue Agency)
centres.role: Emergency reporting. Confirm the regional duty desk and calling access from offshore.

centres.name: India MRCC Port Blair (Indian Coast Guard)
centres.role: Andaman and Nicobar rescue coordination lead where the approved route passes near.

centres.name: India MRCC Chennai (Indian Coast Guard)
centres.role: Bay of Bengal regional coordination contact; not proof of aircraft reach to a particular vessel.

centres.name: Sri Lanka MRCC Colombo (Sri Lanka Navy)
centres.role: Sri Lanka approaches. Direct contacts as printed in the Navy MRCC bulletin of October 2024.
centres.srcname: Sri Lanka Navy MRCC monthly bulletin, October 2024
centres.note: A September 2026 Navy report confirms the centre is active but does not independently confirm this telephone.

centres.name: Thai Maritime Enforcement Command Center (Thai-MECC)
centres.role: Maritime emergency reporting. A domestic short code: establish a tested international alternative.

centres.name: Royal Thai Navy Second Naval Area Command
centres.role: Lower Gulf of Thailand assistance contacts; the naval notice also publishes VHF 16 (156.800 MHz).
centres.srcname: Royal Thai Navy Second Naval Area Command

centres.name: Royal Thai Navy Third Naval Area Command
centres.role: Andaman command call centre: ask for the maritime rescue desk. Continuous duty answering of this line is not verified.
centres.srcname: Royal Thai Navy Third Naval Area Command

centres.name: Thailand emergency medical services (NIEM)
centres.role: Emergency medical activation ashore. This number does not task aircraft offshore.
